name: refusals
description: Every refusal a client has to render, with the status it arrives as and the message key it carries. The keys live in libs/protocol/media.ts so the admin's locales cannot drift from the API's exceptions. Storage says no in three distinguishable ways and a school acts on each differently: `storage-endpoint-rejected` is us refusing to dial the address at all, `storage-credentials-rejected` is the address answering and turning the keys away, `storage-unreachable` is nothing answering. `storage-secret-unreadable` is none of those three — the stored ciphertext will not decrypt, which is our failure to explain and their credentials to enter again. `storage-rotation-conflicted` is two people rotating the same school's keys at once: the database keeps one live profile, and the writer that lost reads what is live now and sends again. `storage-quota-unreadable` is a ceiling stored past what a JSON number carries exactly: answering it would name a different number than the column holds, so it is refused until somebody sets one that fits. Note where each one happens: the quota is refused when the grant is asked for, not when the upload completes — making someone upload two gigabytes and then saying there is no room is not a failure mode we ship. `storage-stream-unsupported` is a bucket that signs one object at a time being asked for a whole catalogue, which only a CDN in front of it can sign. `media-in-use` names the lessons, because 'in use' without saying where cannot be acted on. `media-not-ready` arrives from two places: completing an upload whose object storage cannot describe yet, and saving lesson content that names a file whose bytes are still landing — a file that failed instead is `media-unknown`, since nothing is coming.
